- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is trending up, reduce upward bias — especially after recent spikes — to avoid overcorrection.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and forecast is trending down, avoid excessive downward bias — consider mean reversion toward recent mean if sentiment reverses.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot downward; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast decline by 10–15% in the next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast deviates >5% from true, apply mean reversion heuristic: adjust forecast toward 30-day moving average of prior 10 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, especially after positive sentiment, reduce forecast by 2–3% per day for next 5 days to reflect cooling momentum.  
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often overcorrects — apply “sentiment lag” rule: delay downward adjustment by 1–2 days unless sentiment remains negative.
